aggressive_definition: Lethal prostate cancer, defined as fatal or metastatic, as well as high-grade and advanced-stage prostate cancer.
aggressive_definition_excerpt: From 1986 to 2010, 5861 cases of prostate cancer were identified, including 789 lethal cancers (fatal or metastatic).
study_design: Prospective cohort study (Health Professionals Follow-Up Study)
cohort_total_n_excerpt: In total, 47,885 men in the cohort reported diet data in 1986 and every 4 y thereafter.
reason: The prospective cohort analyzes total incident prostate cancer and multiple aggressive incident endpoints, including lethal, high-grade, and advanced-stage disease.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Calcium intakes >2000 mg/d were associated with greater risk of total prostate cancer and lethal and high-grade cancers.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied RR is for total prostate cancer; the abstract confirms that calcium was analyzed for total disease, although the numeric RR and CI are supplied by existing full-text evidence.

estimate_classifications.endpoint_excerpt: Phosphorus intake was associated with greater risk of total, lethal, and high-grade cancers, independent of calcium and intakes of red meat, white meat, dairy, and fish.
estimate_classifications.reason: The supplied RR is for total prostate cancer; the abstract confirms that phosphorus was analyzed for total disease, although the numeric RR and CI are supplied by existing full-text evidence.
